# ScreenTinker

> Open-source digital signage. A self-hostable CMS and player fleet manager, MIT licensed, with an optional hosted version. Runs on Android TV and Fire TV, Amazon Vega OS, Roku, Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, BrightSign, Raspberry Pi, Windows, ChromeOS, any web browser, Mac and iPad/iPhone (both beta), and e-paper/ESP32 panels driven by a server-side renderer — thirteen platforms, one CMS.

ScreenTinker turns ordinary screens into managed digital signs. A server holds the content, playlists, layouts and schedules; players pair to it and pull what they should be showing. The player is a web page, so a display that can open a URL can run it, and native builds exist for the platforms that need one.

The whole project is MIT licensed and self-hosting is free. A paid hosted version runs the same software on our infrastructure for people who would rather not maintain a server. There is no hosted-only feature set.

## Start here

- [ScreenTinker home](https://screentinker.com/): what it is, features by job (integrations, emergency alerts, enterprise, rooms, measurement), pricing with a hosted 14-day Pro trial (no credit card), and platform support.
- [Guides overview](https://screentinker.com/guides/): every setup guide on one page, by device, plus self-hosting and building content.
- [What is digital signage?](https://screentinker.com/guides/what-is-digital-signage.html): plain-language explanation of how signage works, what it displays, and what it costs.
- [Open source digital signage software](https://screentinker.com/guides/open-source-digital-signage.html): the licence, the data-ownership argument, and where ScreenTinker fits.
- [Certified Hardware](https://screentinker.com/certified-hardware): the device models ByteTinker has tested, what each one does, which are only community-reported, and which are not supported and why.

## Using ScreenTinker

- [Widgets, layouts and transitions](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-widgets-layouts-transitions.html): split a screen into zones, make clock, weather and news ticker widgets, place them in zones through a playlist, and put a Transition widget in the zone it should affect ("every item" in its zone, or "only the next item"). Shader transitions run inside layout zones on the Raspberry Pi/Windows/Mac native player and on Android (from 3.0.1); Roku cross-fades; the web player, Tizen, webOS, BrightSign and Vega draw them full screen only and cut inside zones.
- [Scheduling](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-scheduling.html): the Schedule calendar (dayparting by screen, group or video wall), repeat rules, priority and which schedule wins (a screen's own beats its group's, then higher priority, then the older one), screen-local time zones, per-item schedule blocks inside a playlist (drafts until Publish), and the Preview at… tab that explains what a screen will show at any moment.
- [White-label branding](https://screentinker.com/guides/white-label-digital-signage.html): white-label branding (custom dashboard and player branding), setting a brand name, logo URL, primary color, background color, custom domain, favicon URL, custom CSS, hiding platform branding, enterprise plan requirements, platform default branding, how branding is applied to the dashboard, login page, player, APK filename, data export/import, emails, installed apps (Android/Fire TV, Tizen, webOS, Roku, iOS, native players) that keep the ScreenTinker name and icon, email branding, custom domains and DNS setup.
- [Getting started](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-getting-started.html): the account creation process (hosted vs self-hosted), how to set up a new screen using the onboarding wizard, adding content during setup, checking if a screen is working, what happens after setup, and how to use Simple vs Advanced dashboard views.
- [Content and playlists](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-content-playlists.html): the Content Library (upload types, per-file and per-plan storage limits, folders, tags, Media URL/YouTube/live stream sources), building a playlist (+ Add Content, order, Duration, Play to end, From/To windows, hold screens), drafts until Publish (Unpublished changes banner, Discard Changes), assigning a playlist to a screen (Playlist tab) or a group (Set Playlist...), and the Simple view's Change what a screen shows / Upload photos, which publish for you.
- [Users and roles](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-users-roles.html): organizations and workspaces (each workspace has its own screens, media and playlists), the workspace roles Admin, Editor and Viewer and the organization roles Org owner and Org admin (shown read-only), inviting people (invites last 7 days; without email on a self-hosted server use Add user or the Simple view's invite link), changing and removing members, Content approval with reviewers, and sign-in security: two-factor codes, passkeys, single sign-on and SCIM provisioning.
- [Layouts and zones](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-layouts-zones.html): layouts and zones in depth: which layout a screen draws (head office, then a running schedule's Layout override, then the playlist's layout, then the screen's own Screen Layout), setting a layout on a playlist, per-item Zone pickers and the main zone, the playlist's Default zone for new items (existing items never move), the Move items dialog when a playlist changes layout, the layout editor (snapping, Layer, Main zone, Save goes live at once), Portrait and 4:3 versions chosen per screen, empty zones staying empty, and why a zone has no background colour of its own (use the playlist's Background). Playlist changes are drafts until Publish.
- [Troubleshooting](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-troubleshooting.html): fixing common screen problems: Healthy / Reconnecting / Offline badges and the Recent incidents list, refused or expired pairing codes, edits that are not published yet, schedules that win over the screen's playlist (Preview at… explains why), the time zone coming from the device (Device clock), videos that will not play (MP4 H.264 works best), black or frozen screens (Screen verification, Reload Player), "Waiting for content...", plan limits, self-hosted server URL / reverse proxy / WebSocket problems, and where to get help.
- [Groups and video walls](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-groups-video-walls.html): screen groups (made by ticking screens, then Add to group → Create and add to group), the group bar (Set Playlist, Send Command, Screen off power schedule, Sync, Rules), which playlist wins (head office, then schedule, then the screen's own, then its wall, then its group; editing an inherited playlist from a screen's page makes a private copy), rule-based groups from tags, names, platform and time zone, group sync (Standard to the second on every player type except Roku, BrightSign frame-accurate), and video walls (Advanced view: the canvas editor, panel mounting rotation, wall playlist, wall zones with holds, the Live view, and wall schedules).
- [QR codes](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-qr-codes.html): the QR codes page (Advanced view): tracked short links (/q/<code>) that redirect to an address and count scans, the New tracked link form (Name, Opens), Copy and Download QR (SVG), the Scans panel (last 30 days, iPhone / Android / other), switching a link off (scans then see "This code is no longer active"), changing the destination without changing the code, picking a link in a slide's QR element (Tracked link), what a scan stores (a time and a coarse platform only; bots and repeat scans within 10 seconds are not counted), and the private-address warning on a self-hosted server.
- [Templates](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-templates.html): the Templates page: Installed and Library tabs, Use… to fill in a template's form with a live preview and create a widget (then Add to playlist, a draft until Publish), Slide versus Code templates and the Verified badge, and for server administrators Install, Update, Uninstall, Import… (single templates or an offline catalog bundle) and Settings (community library off by default, unsigned code, extra catalogs).
- [Slides](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-slides.html): the Slides deck editor (Advanced view): new deck templates, the filmstrip, adding headlines, text, big numbers, photos, clocks, dates, countdowns and QR codes, the Content / Style / Motion / Slide tabs, dwell time, background photo and dim, Save versus Publish (Publish makes a playlist named after the deck; Preview plays the last published version), and the optional A.I. Generate buttons.
- [Social feeds](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-social-feeds.html): Social feeds (Advanced view): a feed collects posts from up to 10 sources (Instagram own posts or hashtag, Facebook Page, YouTube channel or playlist, X account or search, Bluesky account or search, Mastodon account or hashtag), shows new posts automatically or waits for approval (Waiting, Shown and Hidden tabs), hides posts by blocked words, age or missing picture, and is shown by a Social wall widget (one post at a time, grid or ticker). Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and X need a connection that an organization owner or admin adds in Settings → Social connections; Bluesky and Mastodon need none. Screens only get posts and images from your ScreenTinker server.
- [Widgets](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-widgets.html): the Widgets page (Advanced view): the 13 built-in widget types, New Widget → type → form → Preview → Save, a worked Menu Board (starters, sections with show times, sold-out items, Square/Shopify or a data source), Duplicate, History (Compare, Restore into a draft, Publish draft), Delete, who may edit (read-only members cannot), saved edits reaching screens without a playlist publish unless approval is on, and plugin widget types on self-hosted servers.
- [Data Sources](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-data-sources.html): the Data Sources page (Advanced view): connectors for Google Sheets, a manual table, weather (Open-Meteo, no key), iCal calendars, REST APIs, CSV files, RSS feeds, Square and Shopify; Test & preview, the slug, copying {{ds:slug.key}} tags into slide text, key columns for stable names, sync intervals, Sync Now, what screens show when a sync fails, and which roles can edit; self-hosted servers refuse private addresses unless OUTBOUND_ALLOW_HOSTS or OUTBOUND_ALLOW_PRIVATE is set.
- [Kiosk pages](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-interactive-kiosk.html): the Kiosk page builder (Advanced view): New Kiosk Page, page settings (title, subtitle, logo, footer, idle screen and timeout), style (background, colours, 2 to 4 columns), buttons with an emoji, label and the Go to page / Open URL / No action choices (Open URL does not open on a screen), linking pages with Go to page and a Back button, adding a page from the Kiosk tab of Add Content (a Kiosk: web page widget, a draft until Publish), and keeping it alone in a touchscreen's playlist so it stays on screen.
- [Content requests](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-content-requests.html): content request forms: a shareable link (/r/<code>) through which people without an account send an image or video, with the places it may show (friendly names over screens, groups or playlists), the dates, file rules (types, size, minimum pixels, shape, video length), days of notice, longest run, requests per day, and who may use the link (anyone with it, a verified email in allowed domains, or the organization's single sign-on); the Inbox where an admin or editor (or an assigned reviewer when approval is on) presses Approve and publish, which adds the file to each playlist dated to the requested days and publishes it, or Decline with a reason the requester sees; the requester's reference number and status link; and the Simple view page Requests from others.
- [Emergency feeds](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-emergency-alerts.html): Emergency feeds (Advanced view, workspace Admin to change): subscribe a workspace to a public CAP alert feed (US National Weather Service by state or zone, MeteoAlarm by European country, or any CAP address), filter by minimum severity, alert type and area, choose all screens, groups or single screens, and show a generated full-screen alert card or a chosen published playlist while a matching alert is live; screens go back by themselves when it ends. Test feed shows what would be on screens now; Recent alerts keeps a week of history. A head office emergency alert outranks a feed. Self-hosted servers need outbound internet to the feed.
- [Alerts](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-alerts.html): the Alerts page (Advanced view, Automate group): alert channels (Slack, Microsoft Teams, Email, PagerDuty, Telegram, Webhook) that send one message per outage after a number of minutes you choose (2 to 1440, default 5), a back-online message only after an offline alert, screen-problem messages from screen verification (blank, frozen, unexpected content, panel off), which screens a channel covers (all, groups or chosen screens), Send test, masked credentials (leave empty to keep), only workspace admins can change channels, the Screen verification settings (screenshot every 30 minutes by default, sensitivity, a problem must last 10 minutes) and the owner's own offline email; on a self-hosted server email needs the server's mail set up and webhooks go to public addresses only.
- [Automation](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-automation.html): the Automation page (Advanced view, workspace admins): hooks, each a secret web address shown only once, that raise or clear an emergency alert, take alerts from mass notification systems (Alertus, InformaCast, CAP 1.2), fire a trigger, write rows into a Manual table data source, or switch screens to a published playlist for some minutes; templates like {{body.headline}}, request signing, GET off by default, Test (runs for real), the Calls log, New address, and the Zapier, Make and n8n API with the Who is listening list.
- [Reports](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-proof-of-play-reports.html): the Reports page (Insights, Advanced view): proof of play for the current workspace, filtered by Device and Start/End Date (last 30 days by default) with Load Report; the Total Plays, Total Hours, Unique Content, Active Devices and Avg Duration cards; Plays per Day and Plays by Hour (each screen's local time); the Top Content (50 most played) and By Device tables; Interactive sessions for interactive web pages; what counts as a play (offline plays sent on reconnect); turning logging off for playlist items (Log plays / Don't log, then Publish); and the Export CSV button, which does not download in version 3.0.2.
- [Triggers](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-triggers.html): the Triggers page (Advanced view): a trigger lets an external system (a Crestron or Extron panel, a PLC, a button) put a published playlist full screen over whatever a screen shows, decided on the screen itself so it works offline. Covers the New trigger form (Fire token, Clear token, HTTP / UDP, Plays, Mode Play once or Hold until cleared, Maximum length, Auto-clear after, Priority, Screens and Groups, Enabled), why only published playlists of uploaded media can be used, the screen's Triggers — listener settings on the Device Info tab (Accept HTTP port 8079, Accept UDP port 7847, Shared secret), the message format (ST1 <secret> <token>, or GET /trigger?secret=…&token=…), which players listen (Android / Fire TV, Raspberry Pi and Windows apps, BrightSign; not a browser tab, Roku or e-ink), priority rules, and the self-hosted TRIGGER_INGRESS server door.
- [Head office](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-head-office.html): the Corporate page (called Head office for store users; Advanced view): turning on corporate playlists in Settings → Corporate content (organization owners and admins, a head office workspace, who can edit), New corporate playlist and Make an existing playlist corporate, local slots with limits and a fallback (Add local slot, Slot settings; changes apply on Publish), Where it plays (whole organization, workspace, group, video wall or screen, with a preview of what pauses), the Store slots report and Corporate airtime, emergency alerts, and the store's view: What head office plays here, Fill this slot, the slot editor and Publish.

## Solutions by use case

Each page says how the feature works, how to set it up, and what it does not do.

- [Solutions overview](https://screentinker.com/solutions/): every use case on one page, with pointers by industry.
- [Emergency alert digital signage](https://screentinker.com/solutions/emergency-alert-digital-signage.html): CAP 1.1/1.2 feeds (US National Weather Service, MeteoAlarm), Alertus and Singlewire InformaCast through hooks, and an alert card that cuts in mid-item on every player. ⚠️ A display channel for alerts, not a certified life-safety or mass notification system.
- [Meeting room displays](https://screentinker.com/solutions/meeting-room-display.html): Microsoft 365 room mailboxes or Google Workspace resource calendars through the organization's own app, book / end / check in from touch screens, ICS read-only. Not a Microsoft Teams Rooms panel.
- [Social media walls](https://screentinker.com/solutions/social-media-wall.html): Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, X, Bluesky and Mastodon with moderation; screens never contact a network. LinkedIn and TikTok are not supported, and why.
- [Digital menu boards](https://screentinker.com/solutions/digital-menu-boards.html): sections, multiple prices, dietary tags, sold-out from a till through the API, dayparted sections, Google Sheet or CSV source.
- [Audience analytics](https://screentinker.com/solutions/audience-analytics.html): camera-based counts of people who looked, and for how long. Counts only, no image stored or sent, nobody identified, off by default; Android, plus Raspberry Pi/Windows with an optional add-on. Check local law first.
- [Enterprise digital signage](https://screentinker.com/solutions/enterprise-digital-signage.html): per-organization SAML 2.0 and OIDC SSO with DNS-verified domains and Require SSO, roles, approvals, activity log, storage in your own S3/Azure bucket, player rollouts in waves. No compliance certifications are claimed.

## Choosing how to run it

- [Self-hosted digital signage: complete guide](https://screentinker.com/guides/self-hosted-digital-signage.html): hardware, deployment, reverse proxy and TLS, running it as a service, and backups.
- [Hosted digital signage platform](https://screentinker.com/cloud-digital-signage.html): the cloud version, what it does and does not change, and an honest account of when self-hosting is the better answer.

## Player setup by platform

Every platform has a guide, and every player is downloaded from the instance that will run it — see
[Downloads](https://screentinker.com/download/), which lists what a given server actually has and says
so plainly when it has none.

- [Digital signage on a Raspberry Pi](https://screentinker.com/guides/raspberry-pi-digital-signage.html)
- [Digital signage for Android TV and Fire TV](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-android-tv.html)
- [Samsung TV digital signage without MagicINFO](https://screentinker.com/guides/samsung-tv-digital-signage.html): uses the built-in URL Launcher, and states which model years actually work.
- [LG webOS Signage panels](https://screentinker.com/guides/lg-webos-digital-signage.html): the .ipk, USB or SI-server install, fleet provisioning and self-update. Community-reported, not certified.
- [BrightSign players](https://screentinker.com/guides/brightsign-digital-signage.html): one autorun.zip built by your own server, dual output, BrightWall sync, real reboots and CEC panel power.
- [Digital signage on a Mac, iPad or iPhone](https://screentinker.com/guides/mac-ipad-digital-signage.html): the native macOS player and the iPad/iPhone app (both beta), autostart and unattended settings.
- [Digital signage on Windows](https://screentinker.com/guides/windows-digital-signage.html): kiosk-mode browser, autostart, and the settings that decide whether it survives a month.
- [ChromeOS and Chromebox](https://screentinker.com/guides/chromeos-digital-signage.html): managed kiosk through the Google Admin console, or unmanaged on a single device.
- [Fire TV Stick 4K Select and HD (Vega OS)](https://screentinker.com/guides/digital-signage-vega.html): these two sticks are not Android, the APK does not install, and they are **not** certified hardware.
- [Roku](https://screentinker.com/guides/roku-digital-signage.html): a native Roku app, live in the Roku Channel Store (https://my.roku.com/account/add/Screentinker; Roku OS 15.1+). Plays playlists, schedules and layouts, but a Roku cannot start itself after a power cut, cannot be rebooted or screenshotted remotely, shows web content as server-drawn pictures, and cannot decode H.264 taller than 1080 pixels. Not certified hardware.
- [Apple TV](https://screentinker.com/guides/apple-tv-digital-signage.html): ⚠️ NOT supported, and not
  planned. tvOS ships no web view, so the player cannot run there and a native port could not show
  widgets, HTML bundles, web pages or YouTube. Unattended operation also requires MDM. Use a Raspberry
  Pi or a commercial panel instead.
- [E-paper and ESP32 signs](https://screentinker.com/guides/eink-esp32-digital-signage.html): no browser on the
  device. The server renders, dithers and packs each frame and tells the board how long to deep sleep; a 304
  when nothing changed means the panel is never refreshed for nothing. Ten panel presets, Floyd–Steinberg
  and Atkinson dithering.
- [LED walls](https://screentinker.com/guides/led-wall-digital-signage.html): there is no LED-wall integration
  and none is needed — the controller presents the wall as one display. ⚠️ Bezel compensation should be
  OFF: LED tiles are seamless and compensating for a gap that is not there crops the content.

## Integrations

- [Templates](https://screentinker.com/templates): the ready-made templates in the signed catalog (menu boards, room signs, KPI dashboards, Wi-Fi QR, clocks, weather), live from the catalog, with interactive previews.
- [Integrations overview](https://screentinker.com/integrations/): every integration grouped by job, and what each needs. Integrations use the customer's own app or keys (bring your own app), encrypted on the server and never sent to a screen.
- [Microsoft 365, SharePoint and OneDrive](https://screentinker.com/integrations/microsoft-365-digital-signage.html): folder sync of images and video through your own Entra app, and PowerPoint, Word and Excel through Microsoft's viewer.
- [Tableau dashboards on digital signage](https://screentinker.com/integrations/tableau-digital-signage.html): a connected app with direct trust; hosted instances need Tableau Cloud.
- [Grafana dashboards on digital signage](https://screentinker.com/integrations/grafana-digital-signage.html): the server renders an image with the Grafana Image Renderer; screens never talk to Grafana.
- [Zapier, Make and n8n](https://screentinker.com/integrations/zapier-digital-signage.html): triggers and actions over the API, and token-less hooks. ⚠️ The Zapier app is private: you push it to your own Zapier account with the Zapier CLI.
- [Offline alerts to Slack, Teams and PagerDuty](https://screentinker.com/integrations/slack-teams-offline-alerts.html): screen offline / back online alerts, also by email or signed webhook.
- [YouTube on digital signage](https://screentinker.com/integrations/youtube-digital-signage.html)
- [Google Slides on digital signage](https://screentinker.com/integrations/google-slides-digital-signage.html): the Cloud document widget for Slides, Docs and Sheets.
- [Canva designs on digital signage](https://screentinker.com/integrations/canva-digital-signage.html): import designs as images or video and keep them in sync with Canva.
- [Power BI dashboards on digital signage](https://screentinker.com/integrations/power-bi-digital-signage.html): the BI Dashboard widget with your own service principal (needs an Embedded, Fabric or Premium capacity), or a public Publish to web link.
- [RSS feeds and news tickers](https://screentinker.com/integrations/rss-digital-signage.html)
- [Weather widget](https://screentinker.com/integrations/weather-digital-signage.html)

## Project and API

- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/screentinker/screentinker): MIT licensed, issues and releases.
- [REST API reference](https://screentinker.com/docs): the OpenAPI specification, rendered.
- [OpenAPI description](https://screentinker.com/openapi.yaml): the machine-readable contract.
- [API catalogue](https://screentinker.com/.well-known/api-catalog): RFC 9727 linkset.
- [How to authenticate](https://screentinker.com/.well-known/auth.md): scoped bearer tokens, what they can and cannot reach, and how a human creates one.

## Acting on a ScreenTinker instance as an agent

- **This software runs an MCP server.** Every instance, hosted or self-hosted, serves the Model Context
  Protocol at `/mcp`. Point an MCP client at it with `Authorization: Bearer st_...` and you get a curated
  set of twenty-two tools rather than 133 raw endpoints.
- [Manage your screens from Claude](https://screentinker.com/guides/mcp-digital-signage.html): setup, the
  tool list by scope, and how it is kept safe.
- ⚠️ The tool list is filtered by the token's scope: a `read` token is never shown a tool that writes.
- ⚠️ Playlist edits are a DRAFT until published. An agent that adds items and stops has changed nothing
  that appears on a screen.

## Reading this site as an agent

- Every published page has a **Markdown rendition**: append `.md` to its path (`/` is `/index.md`).
  Page URLs always return HTML, whatever `Accept` says. Responses carry `Link` headers pointing at
  the page's `.md`, the catalogue, the OpenAPI description and this file.
- `robots.txt` carries Content Signals: `search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=yes`. Quoting and
  summarising this site is welcome; attribution to https://screentinker.com is appreciated.
- ⚠️ There is no way for an agent to obtain an API token on its own. A human creates one in the
  dashboard. An instance that appears to offer one is not ours.
